title: Types of Level Transmitters: A Complete Guide
rank_math_description: Compare the main types of level transmitters: DP, ultrasonic, radar, and capacitance and how to choose the right one for your application.
text:
Types of Level Transmitters: Introduction
 In many industrial processes, knowing how much material is inside a tank or vessel is extremely important. Industries such as water treatment, chemical processing, food production, oil & gas, and power plants rely heavily on accurate level measurement to maintain safe and efficient operations.
 This is where level measurement transmitters play a key role.
 A level transmitter is an instrument that continuously measures the level of liquids or bulk solids inside a tank, silo, or container. The transmitter converts the measured level into an electrical signal, usually 4–20 mA , which is then sent to a control system such as a PLC or DCS for monitoring and control.
 Level transmitters can measure a wide variety of materials including:
 Liquids such as water, fuel, oil, and chemicals

 Viscous liquids like syrups or sludge

 Bulk solids such as grains, powders, or pellets

 Because of their versatility, level transmitters are widely used in industries such as material handling, food & beverage, chemical plants, water treatment facilities, and power generation.
 Quick Answer
 What Are the Different Types of Level Transmitters?
 Types of level transmitters differ by sensing principle, and each converts tank level into a signal, usually 4 to 20 mA, for a PLC or DCS.
 Type Principle Contact 
 Capacitance Capacitance change between probe and tank Contact 
 Hydrostatic Pressure from liquid column height Contact 
 Magnetic float Float follows the liquid surface Contact 
 Guided radar Microwave pulse along a probe Contact 
 Ultrasonic Travel time of sound waves Non contact 
 Radar Microwave reflection from the surface Non contact 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Working Principle of Level Transmitters
 Level transmitters operate using different physical principles depending on the technology used. Some transmitters measure pressure, others use sound waves or electromagnetic signals to determine the level inside a tank.
 For example:
 Capacitance transmitters measure changes in electrical capacitance.

 Hydrostatic transmitters measure pressure caused by the weight of liquid.

 Ultrasonic transmitters calculate level by measuring the travel time of sound waves.

 Radar transmitters use microwave signals to detect the surface of the liquid.

 Despite using different technologies, most level measurement systems determine level using three basic physical principles.
 1. Weight of the Fluid
 The weight of the liquid inside a tank creates pressure at the bottom. By measuring this pressure, the level of the liquid can be calculated.
 This principle is used in hydrostatic and pressure-based level transmitters.
 2. Pressure Head of the Fluid
 The height of liquid above a measurement point produces pressure known as hydrostatic pressure . The greater the height of the liquid column, the greater the pressure.
 Hydrostatic level transmitters use this principle to determine liquid levels.
